Your AI estate is an attack surface. Inventory it.. Shadow-AI discovery is the fastest risk-reduction move most enterprises can make.
Agent tool-call authorization must be separate from user identity — or agents inherit too much.
AI red-teaming with findings-to-fix tracking beats annual pen-test checkboxes.

Where it breaks in practice: product-first thinking — tools purchased faster than architecture is decided, so coverage overlaps in some places and leaks in others while the estate grows more complex, not safer.

The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the architecture-first thesis can drift into analysis paralysis while the estate keeps growing. Zero-trust lands in order of blast radius, not in order of elegance.

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: security here is architecture, not product sprawl — identity-first controls, segmented networks, and telemetry your SOC can act on the same hour. Every program in the Cyber & Zero-Trust domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
